elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: The clause permits one audit in each calendar year, which could allow audits less than 12 months apart across consecutive calendar years.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Only fifteen days' prior written notice is required.
No business-hours restriction appears in the rendered language.

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: Audits must proceed through the F&ASC, but the language does not require an independent auditor.

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: No confidentiality obligation for the auditor or F&ASC is stated.

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: The rendered language contains no off-site audit requirement or preference.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: For a Vendor-requested audit of Customer, Section 9.8 permits Customer to recover its entire reasonable compliance costs from Vendor. No underpayment-based cost-shifting exception applies, so this is at least as protective as the stated 5 percent threshold.

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: The rendered language does not prohibit direct access to Customer systems.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: The added language limits review or audit rights concerning any Party to no more than once in any calendar year.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: The added language requires not less than fifteen days' prior written notice.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: For a Vendor-requested audit of Customer, Section 9.8 permits Customer to recover its entire reasonable compliance costs from Vendor. The language contains no underpayment exception, so Vendor remains responsible even above 10 percent.
